newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end down on Ecuador border worries.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end down on Ecuador border worries.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Wednesday as investors became nervous following a series of local media reports about possible inflamed tensions on Peru's disputed border with Ecuador, brokers said.
While foreign players demonstrated their caution by staying on the sidelines, local investors generally chose to cash in profits gained in recent sessions, they said.
The General Index fell 1.52 percent to 2,126.3 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 1.25 percent to 3,064.1 points.
The absence of foreign funds meant volume was a modest 33.2 million soles ($13.2 million) in a total of 1,961 trades.

Sections of Peru's pro-government media have said that Ecuador has drawn up plans for a possible military incursion into the north of the country. But opposition commentators claim Peru's military has leaked the news hoping to foster stronger nationalistic sentiment within the country.

If the reports continue, share prices would probably fall again Thursday, but in the absence of such news, investors would probably focus on the country's healthy economy and buy equities, brokers said.
"The bolsa was dominated by local investors among whom rumors are circulating about border problems with Ecuador," said Manuel Torres of local brokerage Finvest.

"Also they have started to absorb the news of the country's latest political problems," he said, referring to widespread marches protesting the perceived authoritarianism of President Alberto Fujimori's administration.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru led the market lower, closing down 1.45 percent to 6.79 soles on volume of 758,000 shares.
Peru's largest brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA fell 1.11 percent to 2.68 soles on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- resisted the undertow, remaining stable at 1.32 soles, on volume of 944,000 shares.
